Guy William Rodgers was born on September 1, 1935.
Guy William Rodgers died on February 19, 2001.
Guy William Rodgers was an American professional basketball player.
Guy William Rodgers was born in Philadelphia.
Rodgers attended Northeast High School in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.
Rodgers graduated from Northeast High School in 1954.
Rodgers played collegiately at Temple University from 1955 to 1958.
Rodgers led Temple to a 74–16 record.
Rodgers led Temple to a third-place finish in the 1956 NCAA basketball tournament.
Rodgers led Temple to a third-place finish in the 1957 National Invitation Tournament.
Rodgers led Temple to a third-place finish in the 1958 NCAA basketball tournament.
Rodgers was on the 1958 AP First Team All-American team.
Rodgers was a territorial pick of the Philadelphia Warriors in the 1958 NBA draft.
Rodgers played alongside Chamberlain with the Warriors from 1959 to 1964.
Rodgers recorded 20 assists in Chamberlain's famous 100-point game.
Rodgers led the NBA in assists with 10.4 per game during the 1962–63 season.
Rodgers was named to his first NBA All-Star game during the 1962–63 season.
Rodgers tied Bob Cousy's NBA record of 28 assists on March 14, 1963.
The 1964 Warriors team was dominant in the regular season.
The 1964 Warriors defeated the St. Louis Hawks and advanced to the NBA Finals.
The 1964 Warriors lost the NBA Finals series to the Boston Celtics 4–1.
Rodgers averaged 18.6 points and 10.7 assists in the 1965–1966 season.
Rodgers was traded on September 7, 1966, to the expansion Chicago Bulls for Jim King, Jeff Mullins and cash.
Rodgers played in the 1966–67 season in Chicago.
Rodgers was named an NBA All-Star for the fourth and final time in his career.
Rodgers averaged 18.0 points in the 1966–67 season.
Rodgers handed out a then-NBA record 908 assists (11.2) in the 1966–67 season, which is still the Chicago Bulls single-season record.
Rodgers was traded to the Cincinnati Royals four games into the 1967–68 season.
Rodgers joined Oscar Robertson in the backcourt of the Cincinnati Royals.
Rodgers was left unprotected by the Royals in the NBA expansion draft.
Rodgers was selected by the new Milwaukee Bucks.
Rodgers joined the Milwaukee Bucks for his two final NBA seasons.
Rodgers played alongside rookie Kareem Abdul-Jabbar.
Rodgers helped the Bucks to their first playoff berth during the 1970 NBA playoffs.
Rodgers helped the Bucks to their first playoff series victory during the 1970 NBA playoffs.
Rodgers retired before the following season.
The Bucks acquired Rodgers' former teammate Oscar Robertson and won their first NBA Championship.
Rodgers played for at least two expansion teams during their inaugural seasons.
Pete Maravich thought Guy Rodgers was the best passer he ever played with or against.
Jon McGlocklin, a teammate of Rodgers in Milwaukee, said that Guy Rodgers made every play exciting.
